description: Host tools for AGRO nodes: root-level host installs via sudo, code-server, docker, and desktop tools, and agro workspace create --ref, released as 0.15.0.

userStories.title: Install root-level host tools
userStories.description: As an operator, I want `agro tool install <id> --host` to run a root-level installer through `sudo` so that a dedicated VM can install system packages with `agro`.
acceptanceCriteria: `ToolEntry` gains a field that marks a host install as root-level. Existing entries keep their behavior.
If the invoking user is not root, a root-level host install runs its script through `sudo -n`.
If `sudo -n true` fails, the command exits 1 and prints a message that names the tool and states that it needs passwordless `sudo`. The command changes nothing.
`agro tool list` marks each root-level host tool.
Unit tests cover the root user, a user with passwordless `sudo`, and a user without it.
userStories.notes: Worker commit 99621b34, integrated as 57133ba6. Advisor reviewed the diff: ToolEntry.hostInstallUser "root"; installOnHost probes `sudo -n true` for non-root users, refuses with exit 1 before any prompt or write, then runs the installer as `sudo -n -- <argv>`; tool list shows `installable (root)` plus a footnote. AC1 executed: tool-catalog.test.ts invariant and herdr no-sudo test. AC2 executed: tool.test.ts sudo-n path. AC3 executed: tool.test.ts refusal, exit 1, no installer call, no host config write. AC4 executed: tool.test.ts list JSON hostRoot and table marker. AC5 executed: root, passwordless sudo, and no sudo cases. On the task branch: `npx vitest run` exit 0 (80 files, 1625 tests); `npm --prefix .agro/cli run typecheck` exit 0. Follow-up for US-003/US-004: host uninstall of a root tool does not go through sudo yet; root scripts should use SUDO_USER for the invoking user.

userStories.title: Add the code-server tool
userStories.description: As an operator, I want `agro tool install code-server --host` so that `agro` owns the code-server version on every node.
acceptanceCriteria: `TOOL_CATALOG` has a `code-server` entry that installs for the invoking user, with `hostCapable: true` and an `uninstallArgv`.

The script pins code-server `4.129.0` and checks the SHA-256 of the release tarball: `amd64` `889b09ff3a167a293f53cb68a5a7f38dbab6bd2b50d7a5951c757e56ba51a2b0`, `arm64` `62f7886018923a18cc16112ccfbcd51aee80f8e0c1bb7abc48773d1fd32a7617`.
If the architecture is not `amd64` or `arm64`, the script exits non-zero and names the architecture.
The script extracts the tarball to `$HOME/.local/lib/code-server-4.129.0` and links `$HOME/.local/bin/code-server` to its `bin/code-server`.
After `agro tool install code-server --host` on a Linux host, `$HOME/.local/bin/code-server --version` prints a line that starts with `4.129.0`.
`agro tool uninstall code-server --host` removes the link and the extracted directory.
userStories.notes: Worker commit 6a308f09, integrated as 144ad0c8. AC1 executed: tool-catalog.test.ts code-server entry (invoking-user install, hostCapable, uninstallArgv). AC2 executed: worker downloaded both v4.129.0 tarballs and sha256sum matched both pinned hashes; host run printed "code-server.tar.gz: OK". AC3 executed: install script with a fake dpkg reporting riscv64 exited 1 naming riscv64. AC4 executed: host run with a temp HOME produced $HOME/.local/lib/code-server-4.129.0 and the $HOME/.local/bin/code-server link. AC5 executed: `HOME=<tmp> AGRO_EXECUTION_TARGET=docker-compose DOCKER_HOST=unix:///nonexistent/docker.sock node .agro/cli/dist/agro.js tool install code-server --host` exit 0; `<tmp>/.local/bin/code-server --version` printed "4.129.0 77baee7f… with Code 1.129.0". AC6 executed with divergence: `agro tool uninstall` has no --host flag (existing CLI: "--host and --path apply to install only"); it targets the host when no sandbox is reachable. `agro tool uninstall code-server` in the same host env exit 0, removed the link and directory, and cleared the host record. On the task branch: npx vitest run exit 0; cli typecheck exit 0.

userStories.title: Add the docker tool
userStories.description: As an operator, I want `agro tool install docker --host` so that every node gets Docker Engine and Compose from one command.
acceptanceCriteria: `TOOL_CATALOG` has a `docker` entry that is host-capable and root-level (US-001).
The script installs `docker-ce`, `docker-ce-cli`, `containerd.io`, `docker-buildx-plugin`, and `docker-compose-plugin` from Docker's apt repository for Ubuntu, with the repository key checked.
The script adds the invoking user to the `docker` group and enables the `docker` service.
After the install and a new login, `docker run --rm hello-world` exits 0 and `docker compose version` exits 0 for the invoking user.
Inside an AGRO sandbox, `agro tool install docker` refuses with a message that names `access.dockerSocket`.
A second install exits 0 and changes nothing.
userStories.notes: Worker commits dcdbb13b + repair cfa6616a (advisor review: root-level host installs no longer print the ~/.local prefix and PATH hints), integrated ending at d814009c. AC1 executed: tool-catalog.test.ts docker is host-only, root-level, installable. AC2 executed: tests assert the five packages, Docker's Ubuntu apt repository, and the fingerprint check before the key is trusted; worker fetched the live key and gpg --show-keys printed 9DC858229FC7DD38854AE2D88D81803C0EBFCD88. AC3 executed: test asserts usermod -aG docker "$user" (SUDO_USER) and systemctl enable --now docker. AC4 NOT RUN: needs an Ubuntu 24.04 VM with systemd; deferred to the agro-console node validation (mifunedev/agro-console#168 US-007). AC5 executed: tool.test.ts inside the sandbox with and without --host, and on the host with a running sandbox and no --host, each exit 1 naming access.dockerSocket with no installer run. AC6 executed: tool.test.ts already-installed path exits 0 with no sudo or installer call; reasoned: the script's steps are idempotent. Rendered script: bash -n exit 0; npx shellcheck -S warning exit 0. On the task branch: npx vitest run exit 0; cli typecheck exit 0. Known: host receipt still records the ~/.local prefix (host-config.ts shape); docker uninstall is refused (uninstallArgv null).

userStories.title: Add the desktop tool
userStories.description: As an operator, I want `agro tool install desktop --host` so that a node can serve an XFCE desktop over RDP through Tailscale.
acceptanceCriteria: `TOOL_CATALOG` has a `desktop` entry that is host-capable and root-level (US-001).
If `tailscale` is not installed, the command exits 1 and names `agro tool install tailscale --host`.
The script installs `xfce4`, `xfce4-goodies`, `xrdp`, and `xorgxrdp`, writes `xfce4-session` to the invoking user's `~/.xsession`, adds `xrdp` to `ssl-cert`, and enables `xrdp`.
After the install, TCP 3389 accepts connections on the Tailscale address and refuses connections on the public address.
The script does not change any SSH firewall rule and does not set a password.
On completion, the command prints the two remaining operator steps: `sudo tailscale up` and `sudo passwd <user>`.
The steps follow `https://github.com/ryaneggz/runbooks/blob/main/runbooks/ubuntu-24-xfce-xrdp-tailscale.md`, steps 3 to 6.

userStories.title: Pin the workspace ref
userStories.description: As an operator, I want `agro workspace create --ref <tag>` so that a node's workspace matches the CLI release.
acceptanceCriteria: `agro workspace create [<name>] --ref <ref>` clones `https://github.com/mifunedev/agro.git` at `<ref>`.
If `<ref>` does not exist, the command exits 1, names the ref, and leaves no target directory.
Without `--ref`, the command keeps its current behavior.
`docs/lifecycle-commands.md` documents `--ref`.
Unit tests cover a tag, a missing ref, and no `--ref`.
userStories.notes: Worker commits 1194bdef + repair 2a97b395 (advisor review: replaced a clone-argv runner wrapper with a `ref` parameter on ensureHostWorkspace), integrated as 2bd492d9 + cfd35def. AC1 executed: workspace.test.ts tag case and host-workspace.test.ts argv `clone --branch <ref> <url> <target>` for direct and staged clones; worker also ran real `git clone --branch v1` on a local tag repo, exit 0. AC2 executed: workspace.test.ts missing-ref case exits 1, names the ref, removes the created target; real `git clone --branch nope` exited 128 and left no directory. AC3 executed: no-ref argv stays `clone <url> <target>`; existing create tests unchanged. AC4 executed: docs test for `--ref <ref>`; ste-check.sh docs/lifecycle-commands.md exit 0. AC5 executed: tag, missing ref, no --ref cases. On the task branch: `npx vitest run` exit 0 (1633 tests); cli typecheck exit 0. Note: with --ref, an existing .git checkout is reused without changing its ref (documented).

userStories.title: Document and release
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the tools in a release so that the console can pin that release.
acceptanceCriteria: `docs/installation.md` and `docs/lifecycle-commands.md` list `code-server`, `docker`, and `desktop`, and state which tools are root-level.
`CHANGELOG.md` has entries for US-001 to US-005.
`npm test`, `npm --prefix .agro/cli run typecheck`, and the eval probes pass.

The pull request body has a `## Host install evidence` section with the commands and exit codes of US-002 to US-005 on an Ubuntu 24.04 host. A check that did not run is listed as `NOT RUN` with the reason.
AGRO `0.15.0` publishes the changes.
